---
title: "Choosing a survey tool for research"
description: "What to look for in a survey tool for research: the analysis plan, preregistration, reporting, data ownership and reproducibility, and where surveyframe fits."
---

Most survey tools are built to collect answers. Research asks for more: a
plan written before the data, analyses that can be reproduced, and a report
in a journal's style. These are the questions worth asking of any tool.

| Question | What surveyframe does |
|---|---|
| Can I declare the analysis plan before collecting? | Yes. The plan is part of the questionnaire file, with hypotheses and decision rules. |
| Can I preregister it? | Yes. It writes a pre-analysis plan to submit to OSF, Zenodo or an ethics committee. |
| Can a reader check the questionnaire analysed is the one planned? | Yes. Each file carries a hash anyone can verify. |
| Is a change after collection recorded? | Yes, as an amendment with its reason, printed in the report. |
| Does it write the report? | Yes, in APA 7, as HTML, Word, PDF or OpenDocument. |
| Who holds the data? | You. Answers go to a Google Sheet you own, or stay on your computer. |
| Can I run it without code? | Yes, in SurveyStudio. Everything is also open to R code. |
| What does it cost? | Nothing. It is free and open source (MIT), on CRAN. |

surveyframe does not host surveys for you. It writes 1 HTML file that you put
on any web host, and collects with a sheet you own.
